# PLAN — iteration 1
## Current state assessment
The 8-bit divider baseline passes simulation and meets timing at WNS 0.324 ns and WHS 0.136 ns, using 38 LUTs, 46 FFs, no DSPs, and no BRAM. Since timing is already feasible, promotion requires a strict LUT reduction below 38 while preserving the known top latency of 9 cycles and every defined handshake, reset, and output behavior. No prior proposal outcomes are available.

## Hypothesis
Replacing the separate trial-remainder comparison and conditional subtraction with one widened subtraction whose borrow bit selects the quotient bit and next remainder may reduce LUT use while retaining timing feasibility.

## Instruction for generator
Replace the top’s wrapper-only core instantiation with equivalent top-local 8-bit restoring-divider logic, and add the required `// @latency 9` annotation. In each iteration, compute one 10-bit unsigned difference between the trial remainder and zero-extended divisor; use its borrow indication to select either the unchanged trial remainder or the difference, and to set the next quotient bit. Preserve the existing state, reset, capture, result-register, stall, and retirement behavior exactly; verify that the transformation reduces routed LUTs below 38 and retains nonnegative setup and hold slack.
